sources.label: OSTI IM3 Open Source Data Center Atlas
sources.publisher: Pacific Northwest National Laboratory, IM3 / MultiSector Dynamics, US DOE Office of Science

acquisition.mechanism: periodic re-pull, diffed into Layer A candidates
acquisition.blocked_on: A direct download URL for the current release, plus the release cadence. The CI egress proxy blocks osti.gov, msdlive.org and immm-sfa.github.io, so neither can be resolved from a workflow; both are one manual look at the record page. Until then the snapshot is what it is and the manifest says so.
acquisition.rule: A re-pull never overwrites atlas.csv. It diffs against data/facility_registry.csv and writes the difference to data/facility_candidates.csv, so an upstream change enters through the same gate as everything else.

sources.notes: Largest dataset in the repository and the only one that cannot answer when it was last true. Pass 3 replaces the overwrite with a diff into Layer A candidates.

sources.label: Epoch AI Frontier Data Centers
sources.geography: Global; the surfaces show the United States rows.

acquisition.mechanism: periodic re-pull, diffed into Layer A candidates
acquisition.blocked_on: A machine-readable export URL. Attribution is recorded on the Notion Complete Centers page; the export path is not.
acquisition.rule: Same as the atlas: diff into candidates, never overwrite the snapshot.

sources.notes: 29 rows, 27 of them United States. Capital-cost and power figures are publisher estimates, not filings.

sources.label: Hyperscaler self-published region and campus locations
sources.publisher: Microsoft, Amazon Web Services, Google, Meta

acquisition.mechanism: one config per operator, candidates first, gated promotion
acquisition.blocked_on: Four page URLs and a note on each page's shape (table, embedded JSON, or map layer). The egress proxy blocks arbitrary hosts from CI, so a reviewer has to open each page once, exactly as the PA DEP layer pin requires.
acquisition.rule: First-party pages are strong evidence of existence and weak evidence of location precision. A promoted row cites the operator page and carries whatever geography the operator states, never a geocode inferred from a campus name.

sources.notes: Highest-value unbuilt source: first-party, citable, and covering the operators clients ask about by name.

sources.label: Layer B projects that reached operating status

acquisition.rule: A project whose phase is operational, or whose stated opening year has passed, is a facility. Detection is mechanical; promotion still passes the same gate as any other candidate.

sources.notes: The graduation path the registry existed to make possible. Six projects are currently promotable, three are already in the registry under a snapshot source, one is held.

sources.label: Pennsylvania DEP data center layer

acquisition.mechanism: ArcGIS feature layer, existing permit machinery
acquisition.blocked_on: One layer URL from browser dev tools. Once pinned, configs/pa_dep_datacenter_ingest.json is written and it joins the weekly permit run with no new code.
acquisition.rule: Permits are Layer B until a permit reaches built or operating status, at which point the graduation path above applies.

sources.notes: Carried forward unchanged from the 2026-08-25 plan. A pinning task, not a build task.

sources.label: ERCOT large load interconnection queue

acquisition.blocked_on: The stable report URL from the ERCOT data product library.
acquisition.rule: An interconnection request is the earliest facility signal there is, and it is a request, not a facility. It lands in Layer B and reaches Layer A only through the graduation path. docs/interconnection_queue_scoping.md already establishes that the LBNL queue is generation-only and cannot serve as a facility universe; this is the load-side queue, which can.

sources.notes: Layer B on purpose. Listed here because it is part of the facility-universe programme and because putting a queue position into Layer A would be the exact error the announcement rule already blocks.

note: repo_last_changed is when the file last changed in this repository. It is not the age of the data: a snapshot committed today can be years old upstream. Where vintage_status is undeclared, the honest reading is that the age of the data is unknown, and the surfaces say so.
